prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which enabled incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: All six of us placed B027 first, but unanimity is not the argument. The argument is that it is a complete discovery arc: Holst's gut-hormone and incretin physiology, Drucker's proglucagon-derived peptide and receptor biology, and Mojsov's identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide led to drugs whose benefit is now shown in large independent outcome trials across glycaemia, body weight, cardiovascular and renal endpoints. The science is mature, replicated by many groups and agents, and the clinical scale makes recognition timely. A single-achievement prize with three names keeps the citation tied to discovery of the hormone's action rather than to a product.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide is contested, Joel Habener is not on the credited list and may have a comparable claim, and Knudsen's industrial work on long-acting analogues is decisive for the drugs actually used. Whatever three names we choose, one person with a substantial claim is left out, and a prize that reads as discovery-only may look disconnected from the therapies that changed practice.

responses.point: Sandberg proposes Drucker, Holst and Knudsen so that the prize covers physiology, discovery and the long-acting therapy, and treats Mojsov's allocation as unresolved.
responses.response: I see the appeal of covering the whole arc, but I disagree with the swap. Knudsen's liraglutide and semaglutide design is excellent drug development, and the Nobel tradition in this area has generally rewarded the discovery of the mechanism rather than the optimisation of a molecule. Mojsov's contribution is closer to the biological question of which peptide form is the active hormone, and that question is what made the receptor a drug target. I would keep Mojsov, but I accept that this is the least certain slot in the configuration and that the committee should look closely at the documentary record on Mojsov and Habener before the final ballot.

responses.point: Svenningsson ranks the antisense treatment of spinal muscular atrophy (B001) second, as a clean bridge from RNA splicing biology to a disease-modifying drug, with a coherent two-person credit.
responses.response: B001 has a clearer attribution than most candidates, and the clinical effect in a fatal infantile disease is remarkable. My reservation is breadth. Nusinersen validated splice-switching antisense as a platform, but the discovery rests on one disease target and one drug, and risdiplam and gene therapy now compete with it. I do not think it matches the generality of B027, B039 or B014, and I would not put it in my top three, though it is a credible later candidate.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius ranks TNF blockade (B036) second, arguing that Feldmann and Maini made a clean, mature translational proof of concept for cytokine-targeted therapy in chronic inflammation.
responses.response: The attribution is clean and the maturity is beyond doubt. My concern is that the central insight, that a single cytokine can be a tractable therapeutic target, was rapidly generalised by others, and that antibody engineering and the underlying TNF biology are outside the credited pair. I rank it lower than the cell-therapy and ER-signalling candidates for that reason, but I take your point that the clinical vantage on autoimmunity gives it more weight than my scientific vantage alone suggests.

responses.point: Perlmann ranks the unfolded protein response (B014) second, behind GLP-1, arguing that Walter and Mori make a compact, fair and fully mature two-person prize.
responses.response: I agree that B014 has the cleanest attribution on the shortlist and thirty years of confirmation, which is why I keep it as an alternative. The qualification is that its therapeutic payoff has not arrived, so it would be a basic-science prize. That is a legitimate choice, but it makes it more natural as a second part alongside a clinically transformative achievement than as a competitor to B027 in the same year.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov, Habener or Knudsen has the strongest claim for the third slot cannot be settled from the supplied list and needs documentary verification.
Whether the committee prefers a discovery-focused citation or one that includes drug development.
Whether a second, distinct achievement (B014 or B039) should share the prize, or whether the incretin prize should stand alone.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the provided profile. My spatial-transcriptomics and single-cell work, and my listed co-authorships, do not involve any shortlisted candidate's credited names, and I recuse myself from nothing here.
